Tarikh | Episode 1044 | 19 August 2025
Dogs and humans share a mutual history dating back 12,000 years, as revealed by archaeological studies in Alaska.
A legendary Siberian Husky named Togo led a sled team that delivered diphtheria medicine across 400 km in 1925, saving many lives.
Mahatma Gandhi advocated for controlling the stray dog population, arguing that feeding them was a "false sense of compassion" and that it was a reflection of societal "ignorance and laziness."
